pages.text: "I won't brush my beak! Sleepy!" After dinner, Mumu the little brother shook his head by the water jar. Mom from the mill waved a toothbrush gently in the kitchen. Mumu yawned. "I want to sleep right now!"
Even when Mom offered the brush, Mumu shook his head. "Can't I skip it just tonight?" Beside him, big sister Dodo brushed her beak. Mumu fell asleep without brushing.
But upstairs, while sleeping—huh? Between his beak edges, a tickle! Dough from dinner had stuck in a gap. "My beak feels strange..." His eyes opened wide.
Mom sat beside his bed with a lamp. "Maybe a wiggly bug is hiding in the gap. Shall we chase it out together?" She held Mumu's wing between both of hers.
At Mom's story, Mumu closed his eyes and imagined inside his beak. A gap like a huge valley, a lump of dough, and four purple wiggly bugs rolling and giggling on top. "They made my beak tickle!"

Mom put her beak beside Mumu's head and whispered, "Wiggly bugs hate bubbles." The upright toothbrush was a mill broom, the foam white flour snow! "Brush my beak—sparkle! sweeps them all away." Mumu looked straight at the brush tip.

Mumu jumped from bed and stood by the water jar. A dab of toothpaste! With the brush held in his wing, he scrubbed inside his beak. White foam spilled out. The wiggly bugs vanished in bubbles. Brush my beak—sparkle!
"Aaah!" Mumu opened wide. Rinse-water drops dripped from his beak tip. His beak sparkled and didn't tickle anymore. He flicked his tail once. He did it!
Now Mumu didn't forget. "One, brush when I wake! Two, brush again at bedtime! Three, scrub the beak gaps too!" Next morning, he picked his own from the two brushes standing together.

Mom held Mumu against her chest and touched her beak to his head. "Your beak sparkles like a star!" Brush every day, and wiggly bugs won't come near. Mumu opened his beak wide. "Brush my beak—sparkle!"
